data.name: Renuka
data.gender_notes: Renuka is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Renuka is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Renu' meaning lotus. In Hindu mythology, Renuka is the mother of Lord Parashurama. She is also known as Shakambhari, the goddess of fertility and abundance. The name Renuka carries the meaning “Female form of the lotus” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Renuka usually hope their child will grow to embody female form of the lotus and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Renuka represents the feminine energy of nurturing, love, and fertility. It is believed that the name Renuka brings blessings of motherhood, abundance, and happiness in life.
data.etymology: Renuka belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Female form of the lotus.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Renuka total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Renuka is a significant name in Hindu culture, representing motherly love and devotion. The story of Renuka and Parashurama is well-known in Hindu mythology and is a reminder of the unwavering bond between a mother and her child. The name Renuka is also associated with fertility and abundance.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Renuka represents the divine energy of creation and nurturing. As the mother of Parashurama, she embodies the virtues of sacrifice and devotion. The name Renuka is also associated with the lotus flower, a symbol of purity, detachment, and spiritual growth. The name serves as a reminder of the divine feminine power and the importance of maternal love and nurturing in the spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Renuka, a name rooted in ancient Indian tradition, evokes the image of the radiant and nurturing mother. Her name, derived from the Sanskrit word 'renu', meaning 'dewdrop', symbolizes the tender, life-giving love of a mother that nourishes and sustains like the gentle fall of dew. In Hindu mythology, Renuka is also revered as the mother of Lord Parashurama, the sixth incarnation of Lord Vishnu, reflecting the divine union of motherly love and divine power.

vedic_reference.note: Renuka is the name of the mother of Lord Parashurama.

historical_references.reference: Renuka was the mother of Parashurama, the 21st incarnation of Lord Vishnu. She was a princess of the Haihayas and was renowned for her exceptional beauty. Her father, the king of the Haihayas, arranged her marriage to Sage Jamadagni, who was a great devotee of Lord Shiva.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, possibly between 8th and 4th centuries BCE

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Renuka is in the Mahabharata where she is mentioned as the wife of Sage Jamadagni and the mother of Parashurama. In this context, Renuka is also known as Renuka Devi. She is famous for her unwavering devotion to her husband and her austerities to gain his blessings.

modern_usage.modern_context: Renuka is a popular name in Hindu mythology, known for her unwavering devotion and maternal love towards her son, Lord Parashurama. In modern context, this name is often associated with these themes and is seen on various social media platforms such as Instagram, Pinterest, and YouTube. On Instagram, users may post pictures of women dressed as Renuka, depicting her devotion and love towards her son.
